description: This case covers the digital twin of Cologne/Bonn Airport that Professor Michael Schultz's chair of air transport concepts at the University of the Bundeswehr Munich is building with the airport, announced in February 2025. The twin is a virtual copy of the airport that serves as a test environment for new technologies and processes, starting with models of the airport infrastructure and operations on the airside (apron and runway system) and landside (passenger terminal). At the gate, sensors are to capture the state of ground handling processes, merge them into a situation picture and feed a prediction model, and the aim is to combine realistic simulation with real-time data; emergency scenarios could be tested later in the long-term cooperation, which has run since 2018 and since 2022 has covered dynamic passenger management, data-based aircraft handling and capacity and performance assessment. Coverage is one airport. The university news item is free to read online; the model and data are not published, and no licence applies. Outcome: the twin was under construction when reported, so no measured results are given. Limitations: it is an early-stage cooperation. The case is related to the Simmod PRO airport simulation model and to the Tees Valley traffic digital twin.
